quality.format: One nullable string per reading, comma-separated. The first token without a `kind:` prefix is the source's own quality flag as the source writes it. Every further token is `kind:code`: the kinds a provider publishes beside it (for instance `measurement:T`), `zone:` where the source's timestamps were shifted to UTC, `suspect:<check>` where a plausibility check in the mode `soft` found the value implausible and left it (the suspect level of `source` is flagged in either mode), and, always last, `raw:` where a value was a missing-value marker or a number no sensor can have produced and is returned as null, with the text the source wrote in its place; a number a check in the mode `hard` rejected (the bounds you set included) has `rejected:<check>` before it.

source_flags.description: Quality level of the following columns.
Quality level of the following columns.

legend.meaning: The quality level (QN) of the dataset the reading belongs to, as DWD writes it ('3'). The levels in use and what they mean are DWD's and depend on the dataset's QN column, which `metadata.quality.source_flags` names; readings of a dataset without one have no such token.

The time zone the source stamped the row in, where it is not UTC. `mez`: the stamp was MEZ (UTC+1, the eMD archive of East German stations up to 1991) and is shifted to UTC. `woz`: the stamp is the hour of the station's local true solar time, which is no whole hour from UTC, and is returned as written. Rows stamped in UTC carry no token.

codes.meaning: Stamp shifted from MEZ (UTC+1) to UTC
Stamp in local true solar time, unshifted

legend.meaning: The value is kept, and a plausibility check in the mode `soft` (on a forecast network every check but `floor` and `limits` is; the suspect level of a source's own verdict, GHCNh `Suspect` and 382 `R`, CHMI `Suspect`, is flagged `source` in the mode `hard` too) finds it implausible: one of `range` (a number outside the physical range of its parameter), `elevation` (a station pressure the elevation does not allow), `stuck` (a sensor that held one value, or was dead, over a period), `consistency` (a reading the reading of another parameter of the same file contradicts), `floor` (a model value a little below the floor of its quantity), `limits` (a number outside the bounds the caller set for its parameter) and `source` (a value the source itself marks as erroneous or doubtful in its own quality flag), several joined with `+` (`suspect:range+stuck`). The checks and their modes are the `plausibility` option of the request; the defaults of `stuck` and `source` are soft. No `raw` token of its own: the value is the number the source wrote (beside `rejected:floor` it is the floor, 0.0). Interpolation and summary leave such a value out.

The value is null (the floor of its quantity for `floor`), because a plausibility check in the mode `hard` rejected the number the source wrote, which `raw` holds: one of `range` (a number outside the physical range of its parameter), `elevation` (a station pressure the elevation does not allow), `stuck` (a sensor that held one value, or was dead, over a period), `consistency` (a reading the reading of another parameter of the same file contradicts), `floor` (a model value a little below the floor of its quantity), `limits` (a number outside the bounds the caller set for its parameter) and `source` (a value the source itself marks as erroneous or doubtful in its own quality flag), several joined with `+`. It tells a number rejected by the library from a missing-value code of the source, which has `raw` alone. A forecast network (`dwd/mosmix`, `dwd/dmo`, `dwd/swsmos`) never has one but for `floor` and `limits`: its other checks are soft whatever the mode, so a value is flagged `suspect:<check>` and not nulled.

The value is null, or the value the source documents the marker to mean (no snow as 0), because the source wrote a missing-value marker or a number no sensor can have produced; this is what the source wrote in its place, as it wrote it ('-999', '99.9', '---', '4021'). Also the floor of the quantity (0.0) where a model wrote a little below it (DWD DMO precipitation and radiation), the number as short as it goes ('-0.1' for '-0.10'). After `rejected:<check>` it is the number a check in the mode `hard` rejected, the bounds you set (`limits`) included. Always the last token.
